This discrepancy likely arises from one or more of the following: (1) The Northwestern Mutual Investment Services account ($293,097.73 beginning / $317,374.28 ending, change = +$24,276.55) may include unrealized investment gains or reinvested income that are non-cash and not separately identified in the P&L or balance sheet data provided — if investment returns are embedded in the account balance rather than flowing through the P&L as cash receipts, this would cause a gap; (2) Additional asset purchases, disposals, or other transactions not fully visible in the summarized QuickBooks data; (3) The P&L reports investment income of $14,321.26 (account 4201) which may be partially or fully non-cash (unrealized gains) — if so, a non-cash adjustment deducting unrealized investment gains would be required; (4) Possible transactions in accounts not detailed in the provided data. Management should review the General Ledger for accounts 1002, 4201, and all fixed asset accounts to resolve this discrepancy before issuing this statement.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization founded in 1992 and based in Kansas City, Missouri. The Guild's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking by providing members and the public with access to a shared woodworking facility, professional-grade equipment, educational classes, safety training, and community events. The Guild offers woodworking skills education, safety education, program events, equipment storage, library resources, and merchandise in furtherance of its exempt educational purpose.

Woodworking Skills Education (5001): The Guild offered hands-on woodworking skills classes and workshops covering joinery, finishing, turning, carving, and other disciplines. Total expenses $38,495.35; revenue $50,217.00.

Facility Operations and Member Access (5005): The Guild maintained and operated a shared woodworking facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO, providing members access to professional-grade equipment and shop space. Rent expense $150,000 plus related facility costs totaling $176,016.00; rental income from member space use $26,016.00.

Woodworking Program Events (5003): The Guild organized woodworking demonstrations, special events, and program activities to advance member education and community engagement. Total expenses $12,567.28; revenue $7,995.39.

The organization received fundraising project income of $61,178.50 (QB account 4101) and raffle sales of $2,548.00 (QB account 4007) during the tax year. Schedule G should be completed for fundraising events with gross receipts exceeding $15,000. Preparer should confirm whether Schedule G Part II (fundraising events) and Part III (gaming/raffles) are required based on gross receipts thresholds and state charitable gaming license compliance.
The organization received non-cash (gift-in-kind) contributions of $4,589.67 (QB account 4012 Woodworking Gift-In-Kind Income). Schedule M should be completed to report non-cash contributions.

Prior to filing, a copy of Form 990 is provided to the Board of Directors for review and approval. The Treasurer prepares the return and distributes it to all board members for review at least 10 days before filing.

The organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy, and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121.

Contributions include $4,589.67 of non-cash (gift-in-kind) income (QB 4012) and $2,200.00 of sponsor income (QB 4013) classified as contributions absent documented quid-pro-quo exchange. Preparer should review sponsor agreements to determine whether any portion constitutes exchange transaction revenue requiring reclassification to program service revenue.

Woodworking Rent Income (QB 4006) of $26,016.00 represents space rental to members and is classified as program service revenue. If any portion is rented to unrelated parties at market rate, that portion may constitute unrelated business income subject to UBIT. Preparer should confirm all tenant relationships.

QB account 4010 Woodworking Assets Sold Income of $2,782.60 is reported as gross proceeds from asset sales on Line 7a. Cost basis and accumulated depreciation of disposed assets are not available in QuickBooks data; net gain/loss cannot be computed without a fixed asset disposal schedule. Preparer must obtain asset disposal records to complete Lines 7a-7c properly. Gain is provisionally reported as equal to gross proceeds.

Fundraising Projects Income (QB 4101) of $61,178.50 includes recognition of $27,783.50 of deferred fundraising revenue carried from the prior year (QB 2214 Unearned Fundraising Revenue balance at 12/31/2024). Preparer should confirm gross receipts versus contribution split and complete Schedule G if gross receipts from any single fundraising event exceed $15,000.

Net assets end of year of $452,353.93 equals beginning net assets of $407,394.93 plus current year revenue less expenses of $44,959.00. No unrealized gains/losses, prior period adjustments, or other changes to net assets were identified in QuickBooks data for the period. The difference between QB-reported net assets ($531,650.46, which equals total assets) and correct net assets ($452,353.93) is attributable to a QuickBooks export artifact where the net_assets field reflects total assets rather than equity; correct net assets equal total assets minus total liabilities.

The organization is classified as a public charity under IRC section 509(a)(2) based on its primary revenue sources of membership dues, program service fees, and educational program revenue. The five-year support schedule reflects only the current tax year 2025 data available from QuickBooks. Prior year support data (2021-2024) was not available in the source data provided; preparer must supply prior year figures from previously filed Form 990 returns to complete the five-year support test calculation and confirm public support percentage.
